      "observations": [
        "All17 owned paths and the full812-line diff were read, including the new operation, mock response, tests and every typed-listener call-site adaptation. Historical Ews paths and accepted Exchange/protocol_shared paths are separate phases; the current Rust request/version/Arc plumbing changed later.",
        "MarkAllMessagesRead sends one folder ID with read=true and suppressReadReceipts=true. The detached bridge returns after starting work. A supported server response precedes local DB MarkAllRead, commit and optional window undo. Pre-2013 success instead requests fallback without marking remote items; native code enumerates only locally known unread headers and starts the existing per-message operation. That second success callback filters returned IDs before local updates. The fallback branch does not call AddMarkAllReadUndoAction.",
        "The normal callback retains both folder and optional window with RefPtr until the callback is released. This names the actual ownership interval, not a universal strong-pointer rule or a measured shutdown effect. The simple listener header still describes its Boolean only as resync, although this call interprets it as operation-specific legacy fallback.",
        "EWS and IMAP both restore count notifications immediately after MarkAllRead and before testing its result; rv2 preserves the restore result. The checked base implementation returns NS_OK for the used notification type. Commit and undo checks occur later; no remote/local rollback is implemented here. If local work fails after remote success, the shared handler logs the callback error rather than changing the already-completed remote result.",
        "The Rust enum UseLegacyFallback makes success arguments legible; conversion occurs at the Boolean XPCOM boundary. Sibling create/delete/update/read-status consumers now say No, mark-as-junk maps its existing optional result, and CopyMove maps requires_resync. The enum is not a global replacement rule for every Boolean. The blank line between awaiting the request and validating its response separates those steps in landed code.",
        "The new fake response stores ItemInfo.id, mutates generated message read state and queues readflag changes for sync. It emits only one success response across found folders, and emits ErrorItemNotFound for a missing folder although its comment names ErrorFolderNotFound. The real client warns and chooses only the first response if several exist, so no all-response validation claim is made.",
        "The direct test has nonempty expected-result messages, three unread generated messages, a state-condition wait and a post-sync zero-unread assertion. It uses the default Exchange2013 mock and null window. It does not assert undo, old-server fallback, read receipts, multi-folder partial errors, notification failures or native network behavior. The certificate browser test now waits for unread zero before checking the warning icon; its wait message is descriptive and missing should alone is not treated as a defect.",
        "Bug1990186 complete current0–8 and editor/end controls retained. Its initial request proposes per-message remote update then base local mark/undo; actual source uses the modern bulk operation plus an old-server per-message fallback. Daily/test/uplift and release claims stay historical.",
        "D267689 full creation-to-final timeline, all19 actual current/older inline bodies including submitted suggestion code, and zero summary edits were read. Strong-pointer feedback led to the actual RefPtr window capture; author warned about extended lifetime during network problems and reviewer accepted either approach after reconsideration. No global ownership preference is inferred.",
        "Notification guards, commit/undo checks and the request/validation blank line are present in landed source. MakeScopeExit was suggested but not adopted: the author explicitly chose manual pairing around one database call. Typed-fallback explanation was adopted; do not convert praise or Done alone into a source claim.",
        "Author first planned tests later, then added mock support and a direct test because the new operation broke existing mock assumptions. Later historical failures were suspected to depend on synchronous marking; author could not reproduce locally, added the unread-count wait and accepted it as sufficient to merge while watching intermittents. The source establishes that wait; it does not prove all intermittents fixed.",
        "The final kaie acceptance explicitly says no content review was performed and only patch application was checked. Rebase/vendor conflicts, Try links and the final commit are historical phases; no build or test rerun is claimed."
